title: The Bosphorus Brief — September 5, 2026
overview: A quieter weekend on the ground in Türkiye, but two items merit attention: a fresh US sanction on a Turkish bank tied to the Iran conflict, and a court challenge over inflation reporting that could matter to anyone budgeting in lira. Inflation itself ticked down slightly, though independent estimates remain far higher than official figures. Regional safety news out of Lebanon continues, with no direct implications for travel in Türkiye.
sections: <parameter name="heading">US sanctions a Turkish bank over Iran ties
body: The US Treasury on Friday sanctioned Golden Global Bank, a Turkish lender, alleging it served as a financial conduit for Iran's Revolutionary Guard amid the ongoing US-Israel conflict with Iran. Coverage is fairly consistent across outlets, from Turkish Minute to the Washington Times to Al-Monitor, all describing the bank as a target in Washington's effort to squeeze Tehran's economy. For residents, this is unlikely to touch everyday banking, but those with business ties to Iran-linked entities should note that US enforcement in this space is active and expanding. Separately, and unrelated to sanctions, US visa services in Turkey are reported to have resumed following an earlier dispute — worth confirming with your local consulate if you have a pending application.
